   The Mayor spoke on details/provisions contained in the ordinance
  and his support for maintaining the October 8, 2019 effective date.

  Councilmember Kennedy suggested eliminating the date of
  "October 8, 2019" found in Section 4 of the proposed ordinance in
  order to protect the maximum number of Pasadena residents.

  Mr. Kennedy stated the following for the record , "I have already
  considered the implications [of the proposed ordinance] as it
  relates to my ownership and it would not apply ... "

  In response to Councilmember Kennedy's request, City Attorney
  Bagneris stated that Section 4 of the propose ordinance would
  need to be amended to read as follows: "As applied to notices of
  termination issued prior to the effective date of this ordinance, this
  ordinance shall apply to tenancies where an owner has issued a
  notice of termination of tenancy to a tenant on or after October 8,
  201Q and where, as of the effective date of this ordinance, said
  tenant remains in possession and/or any eviction lawsuit has not
  reached a final judgement or issuance of a final order, after all
  appeals have been exhausted. This ordinance may be asserted
  as an affirmative defense in an lawful detainer action."

  Councilmembers Masuda, Madison, and Wilson spoke in support
  of the staff recommendation and the proposed amendment to
  remove the October 8, 2019 date.

  Councilmember McAustin stated her support of the·ordinance, but
  only if it protects tenants who are being evicted without cause, and
  requested that the term "without cause" be defined term in the
  proposed ordinance. She also asked staff to include language
  related to the presumption of retaliatory action from landlords.

  In response to Councilmember McAustin's request, City Attorney
  Bagneris suggested including the following sentence in the
  proposed ordinance, Section 4: 'This ordinance shall not be read
  to prohibit any terminations of tenancy with just cause, as these
  terms are used in AB 1482."

  Councilmember Wilson echoed the support for staff to ensure the
  Housing Rights Community Center is assessed to ,ensure it has
  the resources it needs to adequately assist the community.

  City Manager Mermell stated that he will work with Housing
  Department and Internal Audit staff to assess the capacity of the
  Housing Rights Center.
